- Fix (built, not loaded; reworked `732902ebb` (local `1472aacf9` before the land rebased it) on the portfolio-monitor session's three findings, each re-measured here):
  - (a) `game_line_bet._margin_for_side` refuses `yes`/`no` before `canonical_team`, so NO path can grade a contract side as New Orleans, `settle_orders`' fallback included (it now refuses there instead of writing an inverted outcome).
  - (b) `kalshi_contract_named_side` strips `^\d{2}[A-Z]{3}\d{2}(\d{4})?` (MLB carries HHMM), and the suffix must be exactly the first or second code (both or neither refuses). Code order is AWAY then HOME in mlb/nba/ncaab/wncaab/ncaaf/nfl/nhl (11-21 ledger: 121 of 121) and HOME then AWAY in soccer (12 of 12); the first version had soccer backwards (no soccer NO rows existed to show it). `canonical_team` is a cross-check only (it misses most college codes).
  - (c) `_check_venue_grade` grades a COPY for "the named club wins" and maps it (`_kalshi_contract_outcome`): a tie or draw resolves NO and against YES, as Kalshi does. This replaces a two-way push / three-way refusal.
  - Stamps `grade_check.named_club`. `_our_verdict` is unchanged and nothing in the check writes `outcome`/`pnl_dollars`. Moneylines only; YES/NO spreads are untouched.
- Result (falsification run 2026-11-21 ~17:30Z, CONFIRMED): the 2:00 AM CST ledger (`C:\SyndicateProd\portfolio_watch\readings\20261121T080049Z\live_all.json`, 39 unique in-game Kalshi NO h2h rows), re-graded offline with the production resolvers in WSL against the fleet data root + Redis (writes blocked). Result: 28 of 28 rows with a readable game box agree, NOP@OKC included (`side_from_ticker home`, margin +6, our `won` = ledger `won`). The other 11 are all NBA games dated 11-10 or earlier, whose box has aged out of Redis; YES rows in the same window refuse the same way, so this is the harness, not the fix. Graded against ESPN's public finals instead, those 11 agree 11 of 11, and the ticker's away/home order matched ESPN 11 of 11. Totals: 39 of 39 translate correctly, 0 conflicts, 0 rows where Kalshi matches the ledger but we disagree. At settle time the box exists, so live coverage is expected to be 38 of 39 (`KXNBAGAME-26OCT23ATLCHA-ATL:no` has no matchup on the order). YES rows: 28 of 28 with a readable box still agree, and none changed for any reason but the box age-out. Tests: 13 new; 190 neighbouring (game_line_bet, paper_settlement*, portfolio side-integrity/resolutions, reconcile, wnba) pass.
- Result on the rework (re-run ~18:20Z, same harness, same snapshot): identical counts. 28 of 28 readable NO rows agree; NOP@OKC agrees (`named_club away`, New Orleans margin -6). YES rows 28 of 28 unchanged. The 11 aged-out NBA rows use the same US away-then-home rule ESPN confirmed. Tests: 18 in the new file, 205 across the neighbouring files. In tests/test_bet_status*, 29 fail (football_props / grader_gaps / ncaaf NCAAF-registry lookups), and the same 29 fail with this lane's code reverted: the worktree has no `data/`.
- Settle fallback (was a lead, now covered by (a)): a Kalshi row the venue has not settled after the 24h grace used to grade `side "no"` as New Orleans; it now refuses `side_not_a_team_in_this_game`. That is the only `outcome`-path effect of this lane: a refusal in place of an inverted grade, never a new grade.
- Memo: `grade_check` is set once per row, so the 36 refused rows and the NOP@OKC conflict are not re-checked by the load. NOP@OKC needs `acknowledge_grade_conflict` (the user's yes).
- Verification: After a web/worker load: portfolio LEDGER grade_conflicts 0 for NOP@OKC (after acknowledge with user yes) and grade_check reason side_not_a_team_in_this_game count for kalshi in-game NO rows = 0 on the next day's ledger.

## 2026-08-17 - THE LEDGER IS A RECORD, NOT EVIDENCE (the inverse of the same day's other lesson)

I relayed *"two uncommitted soccer fixes at risk of being lost"* to the
coordinator as an action item. **It came from a lane entry, not from a
measurement.** `git status` was empty and fix #1 was already on main.

**This is the exact inverse of the three errors recorded above it today.** There
I called healthy things BROKEN from a null lookup. Here I called a committed
thing AT RISK from a written claim I never checked. **Same root cause: treating
a statement as a reading.**

`.syndicate/**` records what was true WHEN WRITTEN. This lane was last touched
two days before I quoted it. **Before acting on or forwarding a ledger claim
about the state of the working tree - uncommitted work, missing files, a broken
service - re-measure it.** The cost here was small (a wrong action item, since
retracted). The cost of the reverse - deleting or "rescuing" files on a stale
claim - would not have been.
